evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking API change. The constant kStreamStallSeconds (120s) was removed and the low-speed stall window now reads default_timeout_seconds_. This is a behavioral change that aligns user expectations with the configured timeout, not an API contract change.
evidence.documentation: Documentation is not affected. The change is internal server behavior; no CLI, GUI, or API docs need updating.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The change is an internal server fix that adjusts when a streaming response is treated as stalled — it now follows default_timeout_seconds_ instead of a hardcoded 120s. No CLI commands, no GUI changes, no new user-visible behavior. Low release risk; no manual release testing required.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None — the get-post-approval-commits script returned an empty list. The merge commit is clean of post-approval churn.
evidence.review: The actual code changes are in the merged parent commit bb39eafc2 (PR #3477 streaming stall timeout fix, authored by @jeremyfowers). That PR was approved by @Geramy on 2026-09-09T22:10:38Z. @Geramy's subject-area expertise includes security and networking (sockets/tcp/ip), which is relevant to the HTTP timeout fix. No post-approval commits were added. The merge commit bc8d99ccf itself contains no code changes — it is a pure merge of main and the release-v11.9.0 branch.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change replaces a hardcoded timeout with a configurable one — it does not expand permissions, add network calls, or alter credential handling. It arguably improves safety by preventing premature termination of long but healthy generations.
evidence.tests: The streaming timeout fix adds a test case in test/cpp/test_http_client_timeout.cpp that verifies timeout=0 now uses the configured default_timeout_seconds_ instead of the old hardcoded 120s constant. Existing test for explicit timeout already covered the non-zero path. No tests were weakened or deleted.
